overview: This bill directs the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that supports small businesses, to do more to promote employee ownership, where workers own part or all of the company they work for, often through cooperatives or employee stock plans. It requires the SBA head or a designee to attend working groups and meetings on cooperatives and employee ownership hosted by other federal agencies when invited or when the SBA has worked with them before. It expands existing outreach under the Small Business Investment Company program, which helps fund private investment firms that back small businesses, so that it also reaches those firms' investors. It also requires the SBA, within 180 days, to carry out its existing employee-ownership outreach duties through its Small Business Employee Ownership and Cooperatives Promotion Program. As of December 17, 2025, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say employee ownership can help keep businesses open when owners retire and let workers build wealth, and that the bill makes sure the SBA actually carries out outreach Congress already called for.
against: Critics say the bill mostly adds meeting and outreach requirements for the SBA without new resources, and that promoting particular ownership structures is not a core job for the agency.
